The diode current equation is given by:
$$I = I_s \left( e^{\frac{V}{\eta V_T}} - 1 \right)$$

Where:
- Forward current $I = 10\text{ mA} = 10 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A}$
- Forward voltage $V = 0.75\text{ V}$
- Assume thermal voltage $V_T \approx 26\text{ mV} = 0.026\text{ V}$ at room temperature
- For $	ext{Si}$, ideality factor $\eta = 1$ (or assumed 2, but standard is 1 unless specified)

Substituting the values:
$$10 \times 10^{-3} = I_s \left( e^{\frac{0.75}{0.026}} - 1 \right)$$
$$10 \times 10^{-3} = I_s \left( e^{28.846} - 1 \right)$$
Since $e^{28.846} \gg 1$:
$$I_s \approx \frac{10 \times 10^{-3}}{3.037 \times 10^{12}} \approx 3.29 \times 10^{-15}\text{ A}$$
proTip: Always state the assumed value of thermal voltage ($V_T = 26\text{ mV}$) clearly when solving diode equations.
